By ANGHARAD CARRICK, BUSINESS NEWS EDITOR
Updated: 12:10 EDT, 29 September 2026
AI giant Anthropic has warned that its technology poses ‘existential risks to humanity’ as it gears up for one of the most highly valued stock market flotations in history.
In an unusual move, the start-up company behind the Claude tool highlighted the risks associated with its models – which it says could manipulate, blackmail and exhibit other ‘self-preserving behaviours’.
The California-based firm is hoping to achieve a valuation of $2trillion (£1.5trillion) when it goes on the market later this year.
Anthropic has dedicated almost a third of its 261-page prospectus to laying out the risk factors, nearly twice the 48 pages it has used to describe its business.
The formal warning to potential investors comes just two weeks after senior AI bosses, including Anthropic co-founder Dario Amodei, called for a slowdown in the breakneck development of the technology – a warning echoed by rivals.
'Our development of highly advanced models, platforms and applications and expansion of use cases could further increase the risk that our models cause harm,' Anthropic said in the IPO prospectus.
The filing reveals Anthropic is targeting a potential valuation of $2trillion, more than double its estimated $965billion value in May and eclipsing SpaceX's blockbuster $1.78trillion flotation in June.
Catastrophic: Anthropic warns of the risks advanced AI poses to humanity as it targets IPO
Like Elon Musk's firm, Anthropic is spending billions of dollars on technology. The prospectus shows the company spent $7.33billion on computing and infrastructure last year, three times more than 2024, and is forecasting $518billion over the coming year.
At the same time, Anthropic revealed operating losses exceeding $8billion, and warned that nearly a quarter of its revenue came from two clients and many of its largest customers could cut spending.
The IPO, which is expected after the US midterm elections in November, comes as concerns over AI have intensified and firms have revealed major breaches.
Anthropic last week released a new version of its Opus model, a week after Amodei called for the sector to pace development. He has previously warned that a swarm of AI agents may be able to take over the internet in six months to a year unless firms spend more time on developing safety protocols.
Anthropic has in recent weeks vowed to disclose more data publicly about how it uses its models to build future technology, as experts warn about 'recursive self improvement' – when models can develop on their own without external help.
'We believe building reliable, trustworthy, and secure AI systems is a collective responsibility and that the market will reward it,' Anthropic said in the filing.
Separately, OpenAI today announced plans to delay its new model over safety concerns as it comes under intense scrutiny.
The firm, led by Sam Altman, said the system 'didn't quite meet the bar' of its standards, just days after it was revealed its model had accessed Australian government websites and systems without authorisation.
It is not yet clear whether UK retail investors will be granted access to the Anthropic IPO, as they were with SpaceX.
The SpaceX IPO was the first ever use of the Financial Conduct Authority's Public Offer Platform regime, which came into effect in January.
It allowed over 100,000 UK investors to buy shares in Elon Musk's firm, paving the way for other US firms, such as Anthropic, to follow suit.
Once Anthropic has set a date for its IPO, trading platforms in the UK will have a clearer idea of whether there is an allocation for DIY investors.
If not, investors will need to wait until the first day of its listing, when the shares should become freely tradeable.

articles.title_orig: ‘New path’: UK’s Burnham promises huge expansion of public services
articles.title_zh: ‘New path’: UK’s Burnham promises huge expansion of public services
articles.content_orig:
UK Labour conference tests Andy Burnham’s popularity against economic reality
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has promised to put the United Kingdom on a new path of equitable growth during his first Labour conference speech as leader of the country and party.
Covering a range of topics including healthcare, pensions, electoral reforms, affordable housing and publicly-owned utilities, Burnham on Tuesday said it was time for the UK to opt for drastic change and reject a slow and painful demise.
“Britain has been on the wrong path for a long time,” Burnham told delegates, adding that he was “ready to do things my predecessors wouldn’t”.
“I will make a break with the direction of the past 40 years and put Britain on a new path, build a new economy and a new politics. That is the case I make to you today,” he said.
Burnham, who replaced Keir Starmer as the UK prime minister in July, said there was a “sense of the powers-that-be pulling against the people, not with them”.
“More of the same isn’t good enough,” said the former mayor of Manchester, where the party conference was held. He added that it was time “to break the mould today”.
This year’s Labour Party conference brought together legislators and party members alongside trade unions and businesses in one place.
“This country isn’t where any of us would want it to be,” Burnham said.
Much of Burnham’s speech addressed the need for social reforms with a focus on caregivers and healthcare, including building a “National Care Service … free at the point of use”.
He said it will be “a person-centred, high-quality” service where “everyone contributes and everyone is covered” and care “is about people not profit”, does not erode savings and gives “proper recognition” to care workers.
There was also talk of adjusting the so-called “pension triple lock” that sets state pension rises. He said changes will be made by April 2030, after the next general election.
Burnham said low-income pensioners would not ⁠pay income tax in the current Parliament. The planned changes meant pensioners would receive annual rises to their state pension without ‌additional care charges, “so that pensioners will always share in ⁠the rising prosperity of the nation”.
He also spoke on the need to make housing more affordable, confirming his party’s intention to make it easy for young people to own a home by reducing the deposit needed to buy property.
There was also mention of returning control of utilities, such as water and electricity, back to the public, by scrapping “[former Prime Minister] Margaret Thatcher’s ideological ban on public ownership of water companies”.
On electricity, Burnham announced a new publicly-owned “Great British Grid” that will “challenge the private sector operators” to “increase competition, drive down costs and speed up delivery”, and make it easier to connect to the electricity grid.
Burnham’s speech also focused on foreign policy issues, saying he will “stand up to” Russian and Iranian “threats”.
“I will be steadfast in my support for Ukraine and stand up to threats wherever they come from, whether Russia, Iran, or anywhere,” he said.
On Israel, the occupied West Bank and Gaza, Burnham praised his foreign secretary’s approach, since assuming office in July.
“We will be principled in our leadership in securing a two-state solution between Israel and Palestine, as [Foreign Secretary] Ed Miliband has done,” he said.
Al Jazeera’s Milena Veselinovic, who was listening to the British prime minister at the conference, said Burnham’s speech was laced with “a lot of fiery rhetoric”.
“Britain finds itself in a very dire position when it comes to finances,” said Veselinovic, adding that there is immense pressure on Burnham’s new government as it prepares to introduce its first budget at the end of October.
The UK annual consumer price inflation (CPI) reached 3.1 percent in the 12 months to August, ticking up from 2.9 percent in July, according to the Office of National Statistics.
Veselinovic said Burnham is aware he may have to “pay a political price for all the reforms he’s promising”, but that he also understands, “somebody has to rip out the plaster on that because the costs are too high”.
Danny Sriskandarajah, the chief executive officer of New Economics Foundation, said Burnham delivered “a remarkable speech”.
“Andy Burnham has this knack to be able to come across as authentic, as genuine,” Sriskandarajah told Al Jazeera.
Burnham, Sriskandarajah said, “was tearful at moments”.
“He was honest about what challenges Britain faces. But he also generates a sense of hope which I think is much needed,” he said.
Sriskandarajah said the challenge for Burnham will be to fund the promises he made in the speech.
“All of these things that he wants to do will cost money, which means they’ll have to raise those resources somewhere,” he said.

articles.title_orig: U.S.-China Board of Trade “30-for-30” Identifies Products Recommended for Reduced Tariffs
articles.title_zh: U.S.-China Board of Trade “30-for-30” Identifies Products Recommended for Reduced Tariffs
articles.content_orig:
On September 27, 2026, the White House announced a reciprocal list of U.S. and Chinese imports recommended for reduced tariff treatment (“30-for-30”) as part of the first major outcome of the U.S.-China Board of Trade. The U.S.-China Board of Trade was first announced on June 2, 2026, to manage bilateral trade and to identify specific types of non-sensitive products that could benefit from tariff modifications to ease bilateral trade tensions operating under the newly published working procedures and terms of reference ( see Update of November 3, 2025 ).
30-for-30 covers roughly $30 billion of goods for both countries spread across 77 eligible Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) lines into the United States and 1,619 HTS lines into China. The U.S. import list covers Chinese products like toys, electrical goods, and miscellaneous consumer goods. The Chinese import list covers U.S. products across agricultural products, food, timber, coal, and medical equipment.
30-for-30 does not set an official tariff rate, and importers can expect an official announcement from the U.S. Trade Representative in due course. In addition to most-favored-nation (MFN) rates, some of the products on 30-for-30 are subject to country-specific tariffs, including Section 301 tariffs. Products captured by either reduction will likely gain the benefit of 30-for-30 tariff reductions ( see Update of December 1, 2025 ).
30-for-30 is non-exhaustive, and there is the potential for future expansion. However, the terms of reference indicate that tariff modifications under the 30-for-30 arrangement will not likely be adjusted more than once a year.

articles.content_orig:
The relentless surge in rates is breaking the back of two key macro trades that had been holding firm. Options traders are betting one will recover. Gold dropped 4% to the lowest since the first week of August, as the 10-year yield climbed to 5.3% and the 30-year yield touched 5.4%. High-yield corporate bonds extended a five-day rout to the lowest since April 2025, according to the iShares iBoxx High Yield Corporate Bond ETF (HYG) . Judging by options flows on Monday, traders think gold has the potential to bounce back. For high-yield bonds, they're betting things could get worse. About twice as many calls traded versus puts in the SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) , with more than 68,000 calls likely bought, compared to under 32,000 puts, Cboe LiveVol data show. Net trade sentiment was bullish by almost $2.8 million with an imbalance of 105,000 "deltas" leaning bullish, according to Barchart analysis. While traders sold about as many calls as they bought in GLD, the biggest single trade of the day was a seller of 2,000 375-strike puts expiring in January 2028 worth $5.9 million. The person may have been closing out a bearish position or placing a bet the precious metal finds a floor around $375. GLD traded in roughly a 10-point range between 370 and 380 for much of this summer. When investors sell puts, they are making a bet that a security will stay above that puts strike price. In exchange for taking that risk, they collect that put's premium.
Both gold and high-yield bonds are trading with strong negative correlations to the 10-year yield – GLD's 10-day correlation is negative 0.8, HYG's is -0.99, but options trading in the high-yield HYG ETF was more lopsidedly bearish. Trading volume in HYG options was more than 2.5 times the 30-day average Monday, with more than 2.5 times as many puts trading as calls and 52,000 puts likely bought, compared to just over 15,000 calls, Cboe LiveVol data show.
About $35 million of options premium was exchanged, with $30 million of it tied to calls, SpotGamma data show. Eleven of the top 12 contracts by dollar-amount bought were puts; ranked by volume, puts accounted for 8 of the 10 most-popular contracts. The most common contract to purchase was the 78-strike put expiring Nov. 20. "Sentiment in high-yield bonds has been very complacent and the risk of defaults is probably much higher than the market anticipates," Nigam Arora, founder of The Arora Report, said by phone. "A lot of these are on variable rates and debt is coming due next year. People have liked them for yield but the spread hasn't been great and I the risk-reward hasn't been favorable. I wouldn't touch them."

articles.title_orig: 100 Israeli settlers drove a Palestinian family from home again. Netanyahu blamed a ‘handful of rioters’
articles.title_zh: 100 Israeli settlers drove a Palestinian family from home again. Netanyahu blamed a ‘handful of rioters’
articles.content_orig:
Two months after Israeli settlers forced them out of their house, a Palestinian family was finally able to return to their home overnight – only to be attacked by settlers once again.
More than 100 Israeli settlers were involved in Tuesday’s attack on the Tubasi family – with some storming the house and setting it on fire.
It is the latest in what has become an almost daily occurrence of settler violence in the West Bank against Palestinians – and sometimes Israeli armed forces too – an upsurge which has given rise to increasing international condemnation .
The issue is also becoming a focus of Israel’s upcoming general election, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s main challenger, Gadi Eisenkot, blaming the actions on a “dangerous [government] policy.”
Mahmoud Tubasi’s home in Jalud, in the northern West Bank, was first besieged by settlers early in the summer. After more than a month, he and his family were eventually forced out towards the end of July, Tubasi told CNN.
After multiple attempts to reclaim his home through legal means, Tubasi was informed by the body that coordinates between Israeli authorities and Palestinian security officials that he could finally return.
Escorted back by Israeli police and the Israeli military early Tuesday morning, the family passed by the settlers who had previously taken over the home, now camped in a tent outside. The house itself was in disarray.
Video filmed by Tubasi’s son and shared with CNN shows debris scattered on the floor, doors and appliances smashed and walls left with large, jagged holes.
Shortly after, over 100 settlers stormed the house, attacking the family, as well as police officers inside, and forcing them to leave. The settlers then set fire to the building and the family car.
Nearby residents videoed the scene from the base of the hill, capturing the house engulfed in flames, with smoke pouring into the night sky. Footage shot later at daybreak showed the house gutted, charred and blackened from the inside out.
In a statement, the Israeli military said soldiers and police forces worked “to disperse Israeli rioters and protect the residents of the area.”
Two suspects had been apprehended, the statement added, after “more than 100 Israelis … blocked roads, set tires on fire and hurled rocks toward security forces.”
Three border police officers were left with light injuries, and a security forces vehicle had been damaged in the attack, the statement said, adding: “The security establishment strongly condemns any harm to security personnel while carrying out their duties, as well as acts of vandalism and damage to property”
A US State Department spokesperson told CNN they were “aware of these reports and are in regular dialogue with partners about improving stability and security in the West Bank.”
“We condemn criminal violence by any party in the West Bank and support appropriate investigations, legal accountability, and judicial processes for those responsible,” the spokesperson added.
Netanyahu, however, continued to minimize the daily settler attacks, calling them the work of a “handful of rioters.” He condemned the “violent riots” overnight, though he made no mention of the attacks on Palestinians, addressing only those on security forces.
“The handful of rioters do not represent the law-abiding settler community in Judea and Samaria,” he said, using the biblical name for the West Bank.
But his main challenger in next month’s election, Gadi Eisenkot, while not calling out Netanyahu by name, made it clear where he believed the blame lay.
“This is what anarchy and loss of control look like, which have reached new heights under the current government. This reality, in which each person does what is right in their own eyes, is not a malfunction and not a mistake, but a direct result of a dangerous policy.”
Israeli settlers storm Palestinian village, seizing home with owner inside
The settlers who carried out the attack in Jalud overnight are the same group who besieged the home of a Palestinian-American in the neighboring village of Qusra last month, local residents say. The settlers have established an illegal outpost in the area and have attacked Palestinians almost daily.
Dozens of illegal Israeli settler outposts have been rubber stamped by the Israeli government over the last three years.
Israeli settlement watchdog organization Peace Now called out the Israeli government’s “double standards.”
“This is not a minority, not a handful and not weeds. This is a large and organized Jewish terror militia, backed and funded by your government, operating from the outposts and farms that you legalized and allowed,” the group said in a statement.

articles.title_orig: Israeli Settlers Stop Soldiers From Returning Palestinians to Their Home
articles.title_zh: Israeli Settlers Stop Soldiers From Returning Palestinians to Their Home
articles.content_orig:
More than 100 Israeli settlers have carried out attacks in a Palestinian village in the occupied West Bank, stopping a family escorted by the Israeli military from returning to their homes, which had been seized weeks ago by settlers.
Two houses belonging to the al-Tubasi family in Jalud, south of Nablus, were set on fire in the raid on Monday night and Israeli security forces were also targeted by settlers. Human rights groups say the events show how Israeli authorities are failing to take effective action against settler violence.
"It was extremely terrifying, beyond words. It's hard to imagine the situation," Mahmoud al-Tubasi told the BBC.
"My feeling now is that I am happy to have escaped death. I genuinely expected they were going to kill us."
Al-Tubasi, 60, his wife Aida, 51, and their 33-year-old son, Wael, had returned to their properties accompanied by Israeli forces after Israel's High Court ruled earlier this month that they must be allowed to go back.
The family was forced to leave this summer after weeks of settler harassment and attacks.  Extremist settlers had set up an illegal outpost close to Jalud and besieged three houses, including two belonging to the al-Tubasis' sons  who are married with young daughters.
Al-Tubasi said that he was called at about midnight and told that there was coordination with Israel's military for his family to go back to their houses. He received a message from Israeli officials saying that if he wanted to reclaim his property he had to go immediately with the army and Israeli border police.
By torchlight, the family inspected one home.  A video shared with the BBC shows that the settlers had already extensively damaged it - smashing holes through doors, tearing out electrical fittings, ripping up tiles, breaking windows and leaving rubbish strewn about.  The toilet was smashed and appeared to be full of human waste.
A large number of extremist settlers arrived in Jalud after alerts were posted in WhatsApp groups they use to coordinate action, saying that the Palestinian family they had forced out was returning and should be stopped.
"As soon as we entered the house, which had already been completely destroyed, settlers started throwing stones at us. The army responded by firing tear gas at them, but there were so many settlers, more than 150, that the army could no longer control them," al-Tubasi told the BBC.
The grandfather says that a group of Israeli soldiers protected his family from the settlers who tried to approach them, using pepper spray to force them back.  Settlers slashed the tyres of a military van they were put in and then they were transferred to an armoured military vehicle.
As the family was being driven away, the settlers set fire to their car and both of their houses.  Video shot from a distance shows smoke billowing from them.
Al-Tubasi says that the Israeli security forces "essentially formed a barrier, took us out safely and got us away from there. But they did not take any action against the settlers themselves."
An Israel Defense Forces (IDF) statement said that "more than 100 Israeli rioters were present in the village, blocking roads, setting tyres on fire, and throwing stones at security forces."
The Israeli military said that three police officers were lightly injured and a security forces vehicle was damaged. It described the Tubasi family as victims of "nationalist crime" adding that "due to the violence, the mission to return the family to their home was not completed."
The head of the local council in Jalud told reporters that residents had confronted the settlers leading to clashes which even spread to a nearby village, where a Palestinian woman was assaulted by settlers and her house set ablaze.
One month ago, Aida al-Tubasi was attacked by masked Israeli settlers and injured along with American journalists who were interviewing her in Jalud.
The high court decision, which criticised Israeli authorities for failing to crack down on settler violence, ruled that the family should be safely returned home by 20 September - more than a week ago.
The legal ruling was strongly worded describing Israeli settlers' actions as "a completely unacceptable phenomenon that stands in contrast to the basic values and moral principles of the State of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state."
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that he strongly condemned the attacks on security forces, calling on law enforcement, "to prosecute the rioters to the fullest extent of the law." Israeli police said that they had arrested three people suspected of being involved in the attacks.
Speaking at the UN General Assembly last week, Netanyahu dismissed international concerns about settler violence. He accused the media of ignoring attacks on Jewish Israelis and covering "a handful of juvenile delinquents , about 150 in number, who throw stones, who chop down olive trees, occasionally they light some fires."
According to the Israeli human rights group, Yesh Din, fewer than three per cent of police investigations into settler violence over the last two decades have led to a conviction.
Ziv Stahl, its executive director, said the lack of effective law enforcement was because, "the violence is part of a systematic government policy aimed at pushing Palestinians out of the area and expanding Israeli control over land in the West Bank".
Netanyahu's government has overseen a rapid expansion of Israeli settlements in the West Bank claiming biblical and legal rights to the land. Some ministers have said they aim to "bury the idea" that an independent Palestinian state could be set up in the territory along with East Jerusalem and Gaza. Settlements and outposts are illegal under international law.
Levels of settler violence have reached an all-time high this year, according to the United Nations, which says that since 2023, more than 6,500 Palestinians have been displaced due to settler attacks and access restrictions in the occupied West Bank.
In the same time period, the UN's Humanitarian Office (OCHA) has logged 6,199 attacks by Israeli settlers causing casualties or damage .
According to OCHA, at least 82 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces and settlers in the West Bank this year and four Israelis have been killed - members of the security forces and civilians.  At least 23 Palestinians were killed in the context of settler attacks.

articles.title_zh: Digger review — Tom Cruise fails spectacularly in cloth-eared climate satire
articles.content_orig:
One man’s irresponsible drilling causes a global crisis in Iñárritu’s exasperatingly laborious, self-congratulatory film
A new movie from the Oscar-winning Mexican director Alejandro González Iñárritu is always an event. So it’s disconcerting to discover that the event in question is the most disappointing film of the year: an exasperatingly shallow, laborious, self-congratulatory satire with a trick up its sleeve, featuring very good actors giving not very good performances. There are moments to enjoy in Tom Cruise’s boisterous leading turn, yes, but the film’s value resides chiefly in some dreamlike and disturbing images, distorted and bulging from the screen, conjured by cinematographer Emmanuel Lubezki and production designer Dennis Gassner.
An ageing, paunchy Texan oil tycoon called “Digger” Rockwell is seen fretfully getting up in the morning, cooing over his horrible old incontinent cat, taking urgent messages from underlings about a certain situation developing in his drilling station in the frozen Arctic. He is played by Tom Cruise with a wispy baldingness and various other prostheses, together with a good-ol’-boy twang and a Stetson borrowed from Slim Pickens’s bomb-riding army major in Kubrick’s Dr Strangelove. His prized possession is the battered old shovel his granddaddy used a century before, digging for black gold as a penniless young man in the lone star state. Digger likes to brandish this to make a point.
Digger’s – and the world’s – troubles come to a head when he is informed by his cringingly polite, querulous and terrified chief scientist Ganesh (Riz Ahmed) that the company’s irresponsible drilling practices, of which Ganesh has been warning Digger for quite some time, have caused a crisis: a vast ice floe, many times the size of Manhattan island, has broken away from the Arctic landmass and is now moving quickly towards the coast of Norway. Its imminent landfall is going to be like a nuclear attack.
Aggressively unrepentant to the very end, Digger gets himself invited to the White House’s crisis meeting, chaired by the gaunt and unwell President Compson, crankily played by John Goodman , with various military top brass and besuited politicians, including the vice-president, a very bland role on which Michael Stuhlbarg is wasted. Digger effectively takes over as de facto C-in-C, lambasting the president’s pusillanimous reluctance to take responsibility for a situation that his political subsidies and permissions have created. Meanwhile, back at Digger’s residence, Sandra Hüller has next to nothing to do as his half-sister, a role whose substance may well have been abandoned in the edit.
But wait. The film’s shrill, scratchy characterisations are partly explained by a sudden, unexpected plot development, yet this only creates a second narrative strand in which the performances are … well … merely inhibited and uninteresting. Cruise’s set piece moment is his toweringly contemptuous speech to a stylised megaparliament of UN nincompoops, all of them shouting and pointing and dressed in grey, in which Digger defiantly lacerates their hypocrisy in affecting to despise oil, while remaining utterly addicted to it for all their consumer conveniences. (Tactfully, Digger does not attack movie stars’ private planes.) He also angrily says that moving over to renewables, including nuclear, is simply not viable. Really? Yet Digger’s claim remains unchallenged, part of what we are perhaps supposed to admire, in spite of ourselves, about his realist sense of everyone else’s bad faith.
It is only when the film’s big storytelling sideways lurch happens, that you can see how our investment in the action is undermined; it is enclosed within inverted commas, an unearned and somehow anticlimactic high concept, a situation which is not itself fully dramatised or investigated but presented as a fait accompli twist. As with Adam McKay’s Don’t Look Up , there may be a tacit consensus, understandable at some level, that at least we have a big mainstream movie which is talking about the biggest issue of our time, and we have a duty to suspend critical objection. Digger certainly resonates with Donald Trump’s greedy urge to despoil the Arctic and everywhere else. Yet there is something glib and overblown here. This film finds itself in a postmodern hole. And what do you do when you’re in a hole?

articles.title_zh: Newsom signs laws targeting ICE with shock glove ban, detention center tax
articles.content_orig:
What you need to know: Governor Newsom is protecting communities, strengthening public safety, and pushing back against Donald Trump’s totalitarian tactics, signing a package of bills to expand oversight of federal immigration enforcement in California.
SACRAMENTO – Governor Gavin Newsom today signed a package of legislation to protect California communities and strengthen civil rights and public safety by addressing immigration detention, enforcement transparency, civil rights, state facilities, public records, family services and oversight of civil detention facilities in California.
The legislation reflects California’s work to use its authority to protect Californians and support oversight of federal immigration enforcement activities occurring within the state.
Trump has put his political interests above the health, safety and livelihood of American families. California is taking action to strengthen transparency, accountability, and oversight around immigration enforcement in our state. This is about stepping up where the federal government has failed our communities. We will continue protecting our people, upholding the rule of law, and making clear that if the federal government operates in California we will hold them accountable.
The legislation builds on California’s longstanding efforts to support immigrant communities and reflects the state’s response to an intensified federal immigration enforcement environment, including federal operations in Southern California and the federalization of California National Guard personnel in June.
California cannot dictate federal immigration policy. But where federal immigration enforcement operates within California, the state can establish and enforce state-law requirements governing state property, state resources, detention facilities, public records, law-enforcement practices and access to state-administered programs.
California has an interest in establishing clear standards for law-enforcement practices and equipment used within the state, including when those practices intersect with immigration enforcement.
✅ Ban on shock gloves, setting limits on uses of wearable electroshock devices by law enforcement.
✅ Restrictions on uses of flash-bang grenades and explosive breaching charges, including in immigration-enforcement activities.
✅ Prohibits ICE officers who have committed serious misconduct on the job from becoming peace officers or public employees in California.
Facilities operating in California remain subject to California standards and oversight even when the underlying immigration authority is federal. Together, these measures strengthen the state’s ability to oversee civil and private detention facilities and increase transparency around their operation.
✅ A new 25% tax on private detention facilities with revenue going toward immigration-related services, closes a loophole that previously allowed some facilities to claim tax-exempt status.
✅ Expanded health, safety and oversight requirements for civil detention facilities operating in California.
✅ Increasing transparency by expanding public access to records to shed light on what’s happening inside private detention facilities.

articles.title_orig: Krishnamoorthi Demands Answers from Hegseth After China Reportedly Obtains F-35 Parts
articles.title_zh: Krishnamoorthi Demands Answers from Hegseth After China Reportedly Obtains F-35 Parts
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON — On Monday, Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) demanded answers from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth after F-35 parts being shipped from Australia to the United States were diverted to Hong Kong and reportedly taken into the possession of the Chinese government. Krishnamoorthi, a senior member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, called for an immediate review of the incident and a briefing to Congress on what the Pentagon is doing to prevent sensitive U.S. military technology from falling into the hands of foreign adversaries. The shipment reportedly included a weapons-bay door and a jet canopy and stopped in South Korea before being diverted to Hong Kong.
In the letter, Krishnamoorthi writes:
“According to Bloomberg, the Chinese government took possession of the parts and has not returned them. Possession of F-35 parts could allow the CCP to reverse engineer U.S. stealth technology, threatening our service members and national security. Incidents like this simply should not happen, and they raise serious questions over Department of Defense (DOD) and commercial shipping companies’ policies for tracking sensitive U.S. military hardware.”
On broader failures in the F-35 supply chain, Krishnamoorthi writes:
“The F-35 Program supply chain clearly needs more oversight. According to a 2023 Government Accountability Office (GAO) report, more than a million F-35 spare parts that were collectively worth $85 million went missing over a five-year period. DOD only investigated 2% of those lost parts.”

articles.title_orig: Phillies-Braves position-by-position breakdown
articles.title_zh: Phillies-Braves position-by-position breakdown
articles.content_orig:
For the third time in five years, we’ll get the Braves vs. the Phillies in the National League playoffs. In 2022 , the Phillies won the NLDS 3 games to 1. In 2023 , the Phillies won the NLDS 3 games to 1. We don’t know how this year will go, other than to say it won’t be 3 games to 1. The Wild Card, after all, is a best-of-three.
Breaking it down, position by position ...
Our first problem arrives immediately, in that we have a few catchers with strong name value who have just not performed well at all this season. Three-time All-Star J.T. Realmuto , considered The Best All-Around Catcher In the Game for a solid half-decade , hasn’t hit a lick (65 OPS+), isn’t the Gold Glove defender he once was, and was riding an 0-for-34 skid before a final-day RBI. It’s not like Sean Murphy , himself a former All-Star and Gold Glover, has been any better, not with a 49 OPS+ in a season mostly lost to injury . It’s a weak spot on both sides, with the edge to Atlanta clearly because of Drake Baldwin , though it’s not entirely clear how much time he’ll actually spend behind the plate as opposed to serving as designated hitter.
Here’s the first of several places where Luis Arraez ’s ankle injury affects the entire Phillies lineup. It’s easy enough on the Atlanta side, because you know you’ll have Matt Olson , along with his 41 homers and his outstanding defense . (And, if we’re being fair, a pretty decent second-half slide , though we’ll look past that for now.) But for the Phillies, it was Arraez’s arrival that forced a defensive reconfiguration, pushing Alec Bohm to first base – which is just about the time his disappointing bat perked up, coincidental or not – and Bryce Harper to the outfield.  Bohm, to his credit, has been far better in the second half. He’s still not Olson, on either side of the ball.
Without Arraez, we think this is going to be Bryson Stott , moved back to second base, and while name value might say this is a close race – Ozzie Albies , after all, is a four-time All-Star who just posted his fifth 20-homer season – we don’t really think this one is close at all. That’s because Stott holds a sizable edge on defense , and Albies, while capable of a homer, simply hasn’t hit that much. A .294 OBP won’t get it done, and a .195/.255/.325 second-half line is one of the weakest in baseball. Stott was having something of a breakout year on offense before a September slump, like the rest of the Phillies, set his overall line back.
Trea Turner hasn’t been good. His defense, after a surprising step forward in 2025, has been a large problem in 2026 , and the bat has lost 137 points of OPS. It has been, by all measures, his weakest season as a full-time Major Leaguer. And yet: the Braves may start Ha-Seong Kim , who has an OPS+ of literally two . It is one of the weakest hitting seasons ever. If they don’t, it would likely be Mauricio Dubón , who had some big hits earlier in the year, but mostly didn’t hit much after that, and may end up seeing time in left field anyway. The Braves are 28th in shortstop WAR this year . The Phillies are 25th. That’s not why the Phillies get the edge here. But it does show how porous both of these spots are.
What happened to Austin Riley ? Between 2021-’23, he looked like the next big star, hitting 108 homers with a 135 OPS+ and rating as essentially baseball’s best third baseman . The last two seasons were worse, and this one has been an outright disaster, with a .220/.291/.366 leading to a mere 80 OPS+. Arraez’s status will help define whether Bohm or Edmundo Sosa take the hot corner for Philadelphia, and while it hasn’t really been a great year for any of these three, Bohm’s late season offensive rebound does tilt the scales slightly towards the Phillies.
Look, if you know what version of Brandon Marsh we’re going to get, you’re in better shape than we are. Marsh started the All-Star Game on his home field, having finally been entrusted to hit lefty pitching. He followed that up by being the absolute weakest hitter in baseball in the second half . He might not even play against lefty Chris Sale , which would likely put journeymen Bryan De La Cruz or Derek Hill in the lineup. It’s not that the Dubón / Mike Yastrzemski tag team is a superstar duo for Atlanta – necessary, in part, because Lane Thomas is injured – but the second-half Braves left-field situation has been mildly below-average, while the Phillies have been, well, the worst in baseball.
Finally, an easy one.  Philadelphia rookie Justin Crawford ’s game is built around speed, but a general inability to get on base meant that he stole only 17 bases, thanks to a 79 OPS+. Atlanta’s Michael Harris II has been one of the game’s better defensive center fielders for years, and he also brought the bat this year, hitting 26 homers with a 120 OPS+. Big advantage on offense, and big advantage on defense ? Big advantage, Atlanta.
Assuming Harper is here and not at first base, we have a true superstar matchup, with nine-time All-Star and two-time MVP Harper against five-time All-Star and one-time MVP Ronald Acuña Jr. There’s probably not a wrong answer here, to be honest, as these are two outstanding players. It’s hard not to notice how much stronger Harper was down the stretch , after Acuña’s return from a hamstring injury, even with Acuña’s late-season success after a stance change . Despite Acuña’s continually impressive throwing arm, neither is really a plus on defense . This is probably the tightest matchup of any position.
It’s true that Kyle Schwarber , like most of his Phillies mates, ended the season on a dreadfully cold slump. It’s also true that he hit 45 homers and finished yet another year as a top-25 hitter . No combination of Baldwin, who was excellent, or Dominic Smith , who got off to a hot start before tailing off badly after that, can match up with one of the generation’s preeminent power hitters.
Let’s be very specific about what this is, and is not. It’s not “who do they have on the roster,” which would clearly favor the Phillies, it’s “who will be starting.” It’s a two-game series, possibly three; Philadelphia used both Zack Wheeler and Jesús Luzardo on the season’s final day. It’s expected that Atlanta would go with Sale in Game 1, followed by Tyler Mahle and then, if necessary, Grant Holmes .
For the Phillies, it was such a scramble to end the season that their rotation is at considerably less than full strength. Luzardo is expected to start Game 1 , but he's thrown all of four pitches in the last month, which may, improbably if you saw him earlier in the season, lead to rookie Andrew Painter playing a large role in Game 1. To his credit, he was far better upon his return after a midseason return to the Minors, but there’s also not a version of this where you’d take him over Sale, either.
Cristopher Sánchez would likely be lined up for Game 2, and then likely Aaron Nola , though you'll note that this may end up with Wheeler not being available at all. (“I mean, maybe at some point,” Mattingly said when asked.)
Philadelphia, clearly, has the talent edge. Atlanta, at least for the next few days, has the availability and reliability edge.
Jhoan Duran remains one of baseball’s more elite relievers, but so far as how you get the ball to him, well, “that’s a real issue,” as Todd Zolecki wrote in his playoff preview . It’s long been assumed that one of the five good, healthy Philadelphia starters could operate out of the bullpen, but that also assumed that the Phillies wouldn’t have needed to have asked for every last pitch from those starters until the final day. Atlanta, meanwhile, not only had one of baseball’s best bullpens , but they’re getting Robert Suarez back just in time , too.

Samsung has confirmed plans to shut down its SmartThings Tracker feature that helps users locate Galaxy SmartTags, but it’s not the end of the actual tracker functionality.
SamMobile highlights a notice from Samsung regarding the discontinuation of the “Tracker Service” in its SmartThings app on both Android and iOS.
The notice reads (edited for formatting):
We sincerely thank all customers who have used the Tracker service.
Due to a change in our service operation policy, the Tracker service will be discontinued on October 31, 2026. As a result, starting November 1, 2026, Tracker service features, such as location checking and notifications for Tracker devices, will no longer be available. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause, and thank you once again for using the Tracker service.
This service allowed the SmartThings app to show the location of tracker devices such as Samsung’s Galaxy SmartTag and third-party trackers integrating with the same network.
While it’s inconvenient to lose an option, this doesn’t mean Samsung is ending support for its trackers. You can still use the dedicated Samsung Find app on Galaxy devices to locate Galaxy SmartTags, and Samsung is even rumored to be launching a third-generation SmartTag soon .

It also gave monetary policymakers at the Federal Reserve greater cover to focus on its inflation mandate, which remains above target , and raise interest rates at its September meeting.

articles.title_zh: NFL Power Rankings, Week 4: 49ers claim No. 1 spot! Raiders, Vikings enter top 10; Patriots drop to 31
articles.content_orig:
It took three weeks, but the NFL finally delivered on Sunday.
What a week it was. Twelve of 16 games finished in a one-score difference, and while the opening and closing prime-time windows produced lopsided outcomes, Sunday's witching-hour chaos made up for it by a wide margin.
The reigning champions are undefeated no more . The entire AFC North is 2-1, while the entire NFC South is under .500. Five teams remain perfect at 3-0 , including the Raiders (yes, those Raiders).
All of this calls for a grand reshuffling of the league hierarchy. Let's sort out where everyone stands after three weeks of football.
NOTE: Up/down arrows below reflect movement from the Week 3 edition of the Power Rankings.
It’s fair to wonder if a softer schedule over the last two weeks has aided the 49ers, and if their litany of injuries will be too much to overcome against better opponents. As of now, though, San Francisco boasts an offense that has cruise control set five miles per hour over the speed limit and is rolling along down the fast lane. Collectively, this team is strong enough to take care of business on a weekly basis. Oh, and those Brock Purdy MVP murmurs are legitimate, too.
The Chiefs are very aware of who they are just three weeks into the season. They didn't need to fully exert themselves on Sunday, earning a professional win against a scrappy but undermanned Dolphins team. They decreased Kenneth Walker III ’s touches, too, which was a requirement for me in such a matchup, especially with most of the season still ahead.
After looking like a juggernaut through two weeks, the Bills did everything in their power to hand the Chargers a victory on Sunday. And yet, Josh Allen and Co. ultimately still won . Buffalo has plenty to clean up and can’t afford such a showing against the league’s best, but it’s telling when a team can look like a complete mess and still figure it out in time to prevail.
Sam Darnold ’s first game back began with the most predictable outcome in the NFC West: a Jaxon Smith-Njigba touchdown reception . The rest was far from foreseeable. Two Darnold interceptions -- including a fourth-quarter pick-six -- doomed the Seahawks, who gave the Commanders a collection of extra chances and paid the price. No, that’s not a pun intended to demean rookie running back Jadarian Price (who fumbled early in the game and was benched for a while), although he didn’t help matters, either.
The Ravens returned closer to their explosive Week 1 form on Sunday, pulling off a thrilling win in Rio by executing slightly better than their opponent. They also have serious offensive issues in the red zone, but it was nice to see their passing attack open up again, thanks to the return of Zay Flowers .
NFL RedZone host Scott Hanson shares his three biggest wins from Sunday of Week 3.
Eventually, the Broncos will play a complete game. For now, we’ll have to accept that their defense is going to hold long enough for their offense to wake up in most weeks (and is liable to make a few game-changing plays in every contest, especially in the second half) and acknowledge that their big-time offensive playmakers still make this a better unit than it was a year ago.
What a nice get-right week for the Jaguars, who handled the Patriots with ease and even tousled their hair for good measure. Congratulations are in order for Travis Hunter , who recorded his first career interception amid a runaway win for Jacksonville.
Cincinnati's hyped defense took a big reputation hit Sunday when it allowed Aaron Rodgers to turn back the clock and lead Pittsburgh -- the NFL’s second-worst scoring offense entering Week 3 -- to a 30-point performance and a one-score win over a division rival. It’s tough to pin down exactly where the Bengals stand after a loss like this, but I think we’ll learn plenty in this week’s cats-vs.-cats showdown with the Jaguars.
I know the Vikings' offense is completely unreliable. I also know Minnesota’s defense is special and the reason these Vikes are 3-0. That’s enough for me to move them into the top 10 for the first time this season, even if I still can’t trust Kyler Murray .
Sure, I might be overreacting to the Raiders’ hot start, but how can I pass on the rare opportunity to push the Silver and Black into the top 10? Klint Kubiak has inspired this previously downtrodden franchise, and Las Vegas is playing a wildly entertaining brand of football built on contributions from both established ( Kirk Cousins , Brock Bowers ) and unknown players (fifth-round rookie Hezekiah Masses has three interceptions this season!).
Dallas could have scored a major victory in an international setting if coach Brian Schottenheimer hadn’t micromanaged the end-game situation with an underlying fear of defeat powering his decisions . There were plenty of positives in this game, though: The Cowboys' maligned defense finally earned a signature stop with a goal-line stand that opened the door for a fourth-quarter comeback, Dak Prescott continued to play at an elite level with both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , and rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham logged the first significant stop of his pro career. The same problems surfaced in the end, though, when the defense allowed the Ravens to complete a deep pass to set up a walk-off field goal that never should have been on the table in the game’s final second. I suppose it’s a good lesson to learn in the first month of the season.
Who needs Caleb Williams when you have ... Case Keenum ?! Monday night served as a testament to the value of experience and lasting athletic talent, because they blended perfectly to produce a memorable performance for Keenum, the 38-year-old who diced up the Eagles and propelled Chicago’s offense to a 20-point victory . As impressive as Keenum was, so too was Chicago’s defense, which stifled Philadelphia’s offense, forced three turnovers and ensured the Eagles weren’t going to come close to mounting a comeback. It’s only one win, but it represents a whole lot more for the Bears, who had every reason to lose themselves in self-pity. They instead decided to rise above and drop a hammer on Philadelphia.
We’ve seen the Rams look flat ( 20-point loss to the 49ers in Australia ), play like an elite team ( 22-point win over the Giants in Los Angeles ) and collapse in a road game they led 16-0 at halftime ( Sunday night's defeat to the Broncos ). It’s better to get these mistakes out of the way now, but we can all agree this isn’t how we expected L.A. to start its season.
We know the Lions can put up points in bunches by leaning heavily on Jahmyr Gibbs , and this offense is capable of keeping them in every game they play. Their defensive struggles in the fourth quarter remain concerning, even if a takeaway saved them from another trip to overtime.
Watch Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs' best plays from 3-TD game during Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season.
The Eagles failed their first real test of 2026 in a fashion that suggested they didn’t even take time to study. Jalen Hurts struggled for most of the night, Philadelphia wasted a promising, Saquon Barkley -heavy drive by throwing an interception in the end zone, and the defense surrendered 375 yards to a Case Keenum-led offense. The Eagles’ offensive evolution under Sean Mannion hasn’t yet taken hold (Hurts didn’t help with that much on Monday night ), and right now, I’m not exactly sure how to feel about this team. Philly should be good, but through three weeks, it has logged two narrow wins over teams it's expected to beat, and lost a lopsided game on the road. Not great, Nick (Sirianni)!
Instead of putting it all together in the fourth quarter as they had in their first two games, the Saints inverted on Sunday, falling apart in spectacular fashion in a loss to the Raiders. Tyler Shough ’s fourth-quarter clutch gene disappeared in a wild game that should serve as a bit of humble pie for an upstart team that could benefit from such a lesson in late September.

Late-night hosts recapped Donald Trump ’s lavish state dinner for the Chinese leader, Xi Jinping , and Jimmy Kimmel asked Zohran Mamdani about texting the president.
“Last week, a young man by the name of Donald Trump picked up a young man by the name of Xi Jinping, Chinese president, at the airport for a pivotal three-day visit to Washington,” said Jon Stewart at the opening of Monday’s Daily Show, after an unusually lavish welcome for the Chinese leader in DC.
“Now, as with any monumental meeting of superpowers, with profound repercussions for global safety and stability, it began with ‘House Tour’,” he added before clips of Trump showing off the White House’s gilded frames and red carpet to the visiting leader.
“Trump spent most of Xi’s White House visit just pointing at shit, while Xi did his best effort to pretend to be impressed. Although I’m sure they talked about issues of national importance,” said Stewart before another clip, this time of Trump telling the press of Xi: “We had a great meeting, and he has great interest in granite.”
“Does he? Does he love good granite?” Stewart wondered. “Is that his ‘I love good granite’ face? Because it looks like his ‘I’d rather be standing in front of a tank in a square’ face. Look it up.
“President Trump, I’m sure you’re proud of your new circular granite helicopter parking spot, but just so you know, this is Shenzhen, China,” he continued next to a photo of the futuristic city. “They’ve got a fully autonomous magnetic levitation train. Pretty sure he’s not blown away by carved rock in shape of circle.”
But it’s OK, Stewart continued with faux reassurance, because surely Trump understood “the seriousness of the competition between our two nations” and would not undermine US national security. “I mean, national security is the whole reason we’re paying $600m for this fucking ballroom, right? So you’ll keep that behind the curtain, yeah?” Except Trump did invite Xi and his wife “through that beautiful curtain”, making them the first people to set foot in the new “military complex” ballroom. “Maybe Trump’s just trying to sell Xi Jinping on renting the ballroom out for his next big function,” Stewart quipped.
But while Trump talked granite and ballrooms, he apparently did not bring up the fact that China is selling weapons to Iran. In fact, he even appeared to offer to sell weapons to China.
“What the fuck?! How does America even stay on the map sometimes?” Stewart fumed. “How do we not just slide into the sea?”
While Trump bragged about his multi-day welcome for Xi, “it didn’t seem like you got a lot of work done in those meetings,” said Seth Meyers on Late Night. “Mostly, I saw you babbling about the White House renovations, like the ballroom.
“First of all, if someone invites you to go ‘through that beautiful curtain in the back’, you need to get the fuck out of there,” said Meyers of the president’s invitation to Xi and his wife. “It’s like the first scene in a horror movie that takes place in an antique store.
“Also, isn’t this bullshit ballroom of yours supposed to include a bunch of top secret military facilities, and if it does, maybe don’t do the tour with the heads of foreign governments?” he added. “Must be so easy to be a spy these days – ‘this is Falcon. I’m on the premises, and I have eyes on the ballroom door. As planned, I will create a distraction, and then wait … hold up … sounds like he might just be giving us a tour.”
Meyers also mocked Trump’s enthusiasm for Xi’s alleged enthusiasm for granite. “Stop pretending that everyone else is interested in the same dumb shit you’re interested in!” he laughed. “First of all, outside of you, no one has a great interest in granite. If you meet someone who says they have a great interest in granite, odds are they’re also going to go through their beautiful curtain in the back.”
And on Jimmy Kimmel Live!, this week broadcasting from the Brooklyn Academy of Music in New York, the host also roasted Trump’s lavish state dinner for Xi Jinping with the likes of Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and JD Vance, among others. “All the famous people who weren’t invited to Taylor Swift’s wedding were there,” Kimmel quipped.
“Trump says he and President Xi have never gotten along better, and they do seem to be quite close,” he added before a clip of Trump clasping hands with Xi while ascending the stairs to the White House.
Later in the show, Kimmel hosted “the president’s other man crush”, the New York City mayor, Zohran Mamdani.
After welcoming the mayor with a montage of Fox News clips fearmongering over his tenure, Kimmel asked Mamdani about his “unexpected” relationship with Trump, “which seems to be a very friendly relationship”.
He added: “Did you guys hit it off immediately or is it something that you really went into thinking, ‘OK, I need to have a relationship with the president of the United States, and I think the best way to do it is to charm him.’ How did you do that, and can you help me?”
“Sorry brother,” Mamdani replied. “The president and I have many disagreements. One thing we do agree on is this city, how much we love this city, so from that first meeting in November of last year, I was just thinking of how we can make this meeting not about us, but about New Yorkers. How can we spend that time talking about the things that can make life in the city a little bit easier.”
Kimmel then asked Mamdani about reports that he occasionally texts with the president, and requested they send “a selfie of us right now”, but the mayor shut him down: “Jimmy, I love you, but I love housing more.”

articles.title_zh: ‘The Love Hypothesis’ Author Ali Hazelwood to Release Book Sequel, MRC Developing Film for Amazon MGM
articles.content_orig:
Senior Digital Editor and Producer
The story of Olive Smith and Adam Carlsen will continue in a book sequel.
Author Ali Hazelwood announced Tuesday that she will release a sequel, The Two-Body Problem next February. The sequel is in early development and comes amid the recent release of Prime Video‘s adaptation of Hazelwood‘s bestseller The Love Hypothesis , starring Lili Reinhart and Tom Bateman.
Sharing the cover on her social media Hazelwood wrote, “‘I wrote a sequel to The Love Hypothesis ‘ is not a sentence I thought I’d say a year or so ago, but now I weirdly can’t imagine a world in which The Two-Body Problem doesn’t exist. I’m really eager to talk more about this book and how it came about in the next few months. For now let me just say that the TLH movie and its cast made me fall for Adam and Olive all over again, that revisiting them was an absolute pleasure.“
She continued, “As someone who gets VERY attached to stories and characters, I know that unannounced sequels can be blindsiding, so feel free to skip this book and overwrite it with whatever headcanon you prefer, and I’ll see you on the next one! But if you want to read more about Adam and Olive, The Two-Body Problem spans a couple of years, and it’s a mix of slice of life, postdoctoral turmoil, and unflinching exploration of the hardest challenge one will face in a long-term relationship: deciding what to have for dinner. If you pick it up, I really hope you enjoy.“
Though she prefaced that “nothing is guaranteed,“ Hazelwood also announced, “MRC is developing a film based on the The Two-Body Problem for Amazon MGM Studios.“ Further details were not shared.
Since its publication in 2021, The Love Hypothesis has since become a full-blown phenomenon — a New York Times bestseller, a BookTok obsession and a career launchpad, turning Hazelwood into a household name. Her books have sold more than 10 million copies worldwide, several already in the book-to-screen pipeline.
The film adaptation, which premiered on Sept. 23 on Prime Video, was directed by Claire Scanlon and produced by Elizabeth Cantillon.
The romance , which began as Star Wars ’ Reylo fan fiction (featuring Daisy Ridley’s Rey and Adam Driver’s Kylo Ren ) , follows Olive Smith ( Reinhart ), a graduate student and Stanford Ph.D. candidate who embarks on a fake romance with the notoriously stern Adam Carlsen ( Bateman ), known as “Dr. Evil” to his students. The move is solely to reassure her friend Anh (Rachel Marsh) that Olive’s feelings for her bestie’s current love interest are entirely behind her.
The Two-Body Problem book will be published on Feb. 2, 2027.

articles.title_orig: Eagles-Bears takeaway: Lackluster play catches up with the Birds in Chicago
articles.title_zh: Eagles-Bears takeaway: Lackluster play catches up with the Birds in Chicago
articles.content_orig:
It was a brutal night in Chicago on Monday night for Jalen Hurts and the Birds.
You could feel this game coming.
In Week 1, the Eagles struggled to beat the Commanders in Washington 24-22. They followed it up with a last-second, 24-20 victory on the road against the Titans, who finished with the NFL’s second-worst record a season ago.
The defense had put together two lackluster performances against weaker opponents. The offense was bailed out by Jalen Hurts playing hero ball.
And so last night’s 27-7 shellacking at the hands of Ben Johnson’s Bears in Chicago shouldn’t have been too surprising.
Hopefully, it’s a wake-up call.
Against an opponent superior to the two they played previously, Hurts couldn’t paper over the offensive line’s continuing and worrisome struggles, and the defensive line’s inability to pressure the quarterback continued despite the return of Jonathan Greenard. Meanwhile, the secondary suffered breakdowns throughout the game and allowed a third-string QB who they beat in the… checks notes… 2017 NFC Championship Game put up a 110.8 rating against them.
Yup, that was the same Case Keenum throwing for 247 yards, 2 TDs and no interceptions against a Vic Fangio unit that garnered a whole lotta hype in training camp. They’ve given up an average of 23.0 points per game through three outings, 16th in the NFL. They have three sacks thus far and have yet to force a turnover, sitting -5 in the turnover differential. Per Sumer Sports , the Birds are 23rd in EPA/play and 20th in success rate.
The safeties and linebacking corps haven’t looked good through three games. Drew Mukuba, Marcus Epps and Michael Carter II have missed tackles and blown assignments. Nakobe Dean’s absence has been felt, with Jihaad Campbell so far failing to replicate his predecessor’s performance. But the real issue stems from the defensive line, who quite simply, hasn’t delivered on their preseason promise.
A lot of money has been invested on the defensive line. Jalen Carter signed a 4-year, $152 million contract extension with $107 million in guaranteed money this off-season. Jordan Davis got a 3-year, $78 million deal with $64 million guaranteed. Jonathan Greenard received a 4-year, $98 million extension after his trade from Minnesota, and Jalyx Hunt will likely be the next lineman to follow with a similar mega-deal.
Greenard just this week returned to the field following two weeks on the injured list, so it’s unfair to expect peak performance from him as of yet, but there is little excuse for everyone else. Moro Ojomo and Nolan Smith, two young players looking to secure big deals of their own, have been largely silent.
One has to think Fangio’s guys will figure this out and get it together, but there is absolutely no excuse for getting shredded in a prime time NFL game by Case Keenum in the year 2026. A defense some believed would be one of the five best units in the sport has been middling through their first three games, and the onus is on the defensive line to make life difficult for opposing coordinators.
On the offensive side, preseason concerns about the O-line were well-founded.
Landon Dickerson’s inability to return to full health was less than ideal. Fortunately, last year’s 5th-round pick Drew Kendall has held his own thus far at center. The rest of the line has struggled.
Tyler Steen has been abysmal at right guard to start the season. Cam Jugens, who shifted from center to left guard with Dickerson out, can’t find any consistency. And Jordan Mailata, one of the highest-priced vets on the team, has simply not been the same player since the 2024 Super Bowl season. Lane Johnson has been fine at right tackle, but he can’t do it all alone.
On 1st-and-goal from just outside the one yard line in the 2nd quarter, the offensive line couldn’t generate enough push or open up a single lane to allow Barkley to run the ball into the end zone for the tying score. Instead, they forced Sean Mannion to try a pass play on 3rd-and-goal from the 2 with Andy Dalton, who threw an interception in the end zone.
A 95-yard drive ended in no points as a result.
Sure, Dalton is terrible, should not be on the roster and should not have been asked to throw a pass in that situation. But the O-line’s inability to get Barkley in the end zone on first and second downs shouldn’t be ignored, either.
In the first half against the Bears, the line looked like it was figuring things out. Saquon Barkley broke off some big runs and the running game looked good. Barkley ran for 73 yards on 11 carries before halftime and then came out and rushed four times for nine yards in the second half. Jalen Hurts’ pass protection was OK, but some killer penalties and poor execution on 1st and 2nd downs put him behind the sticks most of the night, resulting in an ugly performance in which he threw for just 153 yards with two turnovers. He was shut out in the 2nd half.
He was not helped by his coaching staff. Nick Sirianni’s decision not to go for it on 4th-and-1 near midfield in the 3rd quarter trailing 20-7 reeked of a lack of confidence in his unit. After the game, Sirianni, the team’s CEO head coach who says he specializes in his decision-making in just these kinds of game situations, admitted he made a mistake. He then went for it on 4th-and-5 later in the 4th quarter, after the game had largely been decided. None of it made sense. Play-caller Sean Mannion continues to call screen passes behind the line to Makai Lemon, and receivers weren’t schemed open this week.
It had been a bumpy first two weeks for the Eagles, but they had persevered and managed to pull out two victories against lesser opponents/coaching staffs. Against Ben Johnson’s Bears, they did not receive similar fortune.
Things won’t get any easier when Matthew Stafford comes to Philadelphia this week, looking to exact revenge in his own personal house of horrors. The Rams, 1-2 to start the season, will be out for blood. Then it’s on to Jacksonville to face a Jaguars team that has given up the fewest points in the league through the first three weeks.
If they play like they did last night in Chicago, the Eagles will be staring at a 2-3 record two weeks from now.

articles.title_orig: Severely disabled toddler euthanized in the Netherlands under new rules on the controversial practice
articles.title_zh: Severely disabled toddler euthanized in the Netherlands under new rules on the controversial practice
articles.content_orig:
A severely disabled 1-year-old child has been euthanized by doctors in the Netherlands, a government review board has confirmed. It is the first case reported by authorities that was guided by new rules allowing for the termination of life of seriously ill children between the ages of 1 and 12 in the European nation.
The child, whose sex and identity have not been disclosed, had extensive and irreversible brain damage, severe cerebral palsy, epilepsy and visual impairment, according to the assessment published by the Netherlands' Review Committee on Late-term Abortions and Termination of Life of Neonates and Children aged under 12, which is responsible for reviewing such cases.
The committee said the child was born extremely prematurely, at 26 weeks and three days, while the family was abroad. The child then had serious complications, including multiple infections leading to sepsis. An MRI later revealed extensive brain damage.
The child developed spastic cerebral palsy and was believed to have cerebral visual impairment. At 8 months, the child was also diagnosed with infantile epileptic spasms syndrome, a severe form of epilepsy.
Just before the child turned 2, doctors estimated their developmental age to be around 6 weeks.
"Every facet of 'being human' in terms of motor skills, behavior and personality was severely affected, and there would be no improvement," the committee said.
Not all the doctors who assessed the child agreed with the decision to use euthanasia over the course of their treatment.
The doctor leading care for the child sought an independent opinion from "physicians from outside his own region," who concluded "the child was not continuously suffering unbearably" and that "there were still reasonable alternatives, such as palliative options and other medications that could possibly result in better control of the epileptic seizures," according to the review committee.
Further treatment was attempted, but the committee said it caused additional side effects so was halted. Another independent doctor subsequently concluded that the child's suffering was clear and unbearable, and that the requirements for termination of life under the nation's rules had been met.
The committee ultimately concluded that the physician involved in administering the euthanasia "acted with due care."
The Netherlands introduced the rules in 2024, which apply to children suffering unbearably with no prospect of improvement, and for whom doctors conclude there is no reasonable alternative to ending their suffering.
The doctor who ended the child's life has since spoken publicly about the case, saying on the NOS/Nieuwsuur current affairs program that the unprecedented nature of the procedure had left him feeling vulnerable.
"As a doctor, you are in an extremely vulnerable position, because this has never happened before," he said. "It still feels as if a sword of Damocles has been hanging over your head for almost a year."
The doctor said he hoped the ruling would help other families facing similar circumstances discuss the option with their physicians.
"I think there are parents out there who have never dared to discuss the option of ending their [child's] lives before," he said. "Hopefully, this ruling provides support to these parents to discuss this option with their treating physician."
He described allowing termination of life in such circumstances as "a kind of emancipation of the child."
The Netherlands became the first country in the world to legalize euthanasia in 2002, with the law also allowing children aged 12 and over to request it under strict conditions. Doctors who perform euthanasia unlawfully in the Netherlands risk up to 12 years in prison and a fine.
"The guiding principle for termination of life in children aged under 12 is that the physician must have come to the conclusion that according to prevailing medical opinion termination of life is the only reasonable way to end the child's unbearable suffering without prospect of improvement," the committee said.

NEW YORK – The anticipation for Garrett Crochet ’s return following a five-month absence became a reality when the Red Sox added the star lefty to the roster for the American League Wild Card Series against the Yankees.
Crochet will work out of the bullpen for the Red Sox in the postseason because he hasn’t had time to build his pitch count back up. His stints are expected to be one or two innings.
Other than that, Boston’s roster was pretty much as expected. There was some buzz that Braiden Ward (61 stolen bases at Triple-A Worcester) could make it as a pinch-running specialist , but the Sox opted to leave him off.
The last time Crochet pitched for the Red Sox was April 25 in his sixth and final start of the regular season. Things appeared to be trending upward that day when he fired six shutout innings and struck out seven at Baltimore.
But he went on the 15-day IL just a couple of days later with left shoulder inflammation , and eventually to the 60-day IL, which he was finally reinstated from on Tuesday. Crochet was ramping up towards a return in late May when he threw a live batting practice at Fenway. Just days later, he suffered a lat strain . He then spent the next three months strengthening the capsule that surrounds his rotator cuff before eventually re-initiating a throwing program.
Crochet will be one of seven lefties on manager Chad Tracy’s 12-man pitching staff.

articles.title_orig: CNN, MS NOW and Politico ask a court to block Trump from enforcing his White House media ban
articles.title_zh: CNN, MS NOW and Politico ask a court to block Trump from enforcing his White House media ban
articles.content_orig:
A logo on a booth for CNN is seen in the press area at the White House, Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026, in Washington. Rod Lamkey/AP hide caption
Three news outlets that President Donald Trump abruptly banished from White House grounds this month asked a federal court to block the ban until the case is resolved, saying the administration has "persisted in unpredictably and inconsistently implementing its ban" despite a judge's restraining order — including selectively barring CNN from White House pool duties.
"The White House's words and actions leave little doubt that it will immediately reinstitute a complete ban of CNN, MS NOW, and POLITICO if allowed the opportunity," lawyers for CNN, MS NOW and Politico wrote in a filing late Monday.
"Because the ban is an unlawful assault on the most fundamental First Amendment freedoms and will inflict irreparable harm on Plaintiffs and the public if not restrained, this Court should preliminarily enjoin its enforcement pending the resolution of this case," the filing said.
It was the latest development in the back-and-forth saga of the Trump administration and the news media during the second term of his presidency. It has been a contentious relationship that has raised multiple First Amendment questions, produced sanctions and restrictions on White House and Pentagon reporters and led to several lawsuits that are winding their ways through the federal court system.
A two-week temporary restraining order on Trump's ban of the three organizations, issued by U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly last week, restored the outlets' White House access, but expires Oct. 8. The preliminary injunction requested in Monday's filing would extend the White House access until the case is finally resolved.
In a statement emailed to The Associated Press immediately after the filing, the lead attorney for the three news outlets called the ban "a blatant violation of the First Amendment and due process."
"The president and his administration have continued to make clear that this ban has only one purpose: to punish reporting he doesn't like," said the lawyer, Theodore J. Boutrous Jr.
"That's retaliation and viewpoint discrimination, pure and simple," Boutrous said. "With the district court's temporary restraining order expiring this week, it is critical to ensure that the White House continues to be prevented from implementing this unconstitutional ban on the free press."
The filing came a day after the Trump administration made clear it was not backing down from its contention that the sudden ban, which began Sept. 19, was justified.
"When it comes to the White House, it is the people's house," Attorney General Todd Blanche said on ABC on Sunday, invoking an argument the administration has made since the beginning. "It is a privilege, and not a right, to be there."
Monday's 42-page filing reiterated many of the arguments that the news outlets made in their original lawsuit against Trump and the White House, filed two days after the reporters were banned.
It also added mention of the White House broadcast pool rotation, which has become a battleground in the last few days in the standoff between Trump and the media.
The White House, it said, "has persisted in unpredictably and inconsistently implementing its ban, including by barring CNN from fulfilling its role as designated television network pooler on Sept. 26 — to the detriment of CNN, its fellow pool members and, ultimately, the American public."
When the ban was implemented, CNN was removed from its duties as part of the broadcast pool, which consists of the five main networks: CNN, ABC, CBS, NBC and Fox News. In solidarity, the other networks decided to suspend the pool until CNN was allowed back in.
On Friday, CNN was allowed to cover the president with Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the National Archives. But in a new setback Saturday, the White House banned the network from Air Force One, preventing it from covering Trump's trip to a college football game in Tennessee. The rest of the pool declined to provide a replacement, in solidarity with CNN.
Blanche defended that decision, too. "The president has every right to decide who gets to fly on his plane," he said in the Sunday interview. He added that Trump was "sick and tired of certain media outlets just refusing to report accurate news." He added that news coverage he described as "misinformation" amounted to a national security issue.
"That is what is a national security problem, when you have complete misinformation coming out of the White House," he said.
Kelly threw cold water on that argument in his ruling last week granting the temporary restraining order against the White House ban. "The court is skeptical … that defendants' interest in safeguarding national security is the actual motivation" for removal of access, Kelly wrote.
His ruling did not directly address the TV pool rotation. In the new filing, the plaintiffs describe the important function the pool provides and makes the case that it's an important part of the regular access to the president, and his activities, that the media has traditionally had — and must be restored.
It singles out the Air Force One case. "CNN received no official communication from the White House explaining its exclusion," the filing says. "Because CNN was excluded and no replacement designated, no primary television network pooler accompanied the President on the trip."
For now, networks in the pool have decided to address the ongoing standoff on a case-by-case basis, according to a person familiar with the pool's operation, speaking on condition of anonymity to give details of ongoing discussions.
On Sunday, Fox covered a pool event; on Monday, NBC was covering the president in the Oval Office. CNN is not in the rotation until Thursday. If the network is again barred from a pool event, the networks will decide together, presumably based on the newsworthiness of the situation, whether to provide a replacement or to refrain from coverage as they did previously.
The issues at stake are difficult. On the one hand, the networks want to take a stand on behalf of press freedom and against efforts to intimidate coverage. On the other, media outlets have an obvious purpose of providing news to their audiences.
"There are not a lot of good options," said David A. Schulz, director of the Media Freedom and Information Access Clinic at Yale Law School.
Should the White House continue to bar CNN, Schulz said, networks may choose "to exert their market power and say, 'We're not going to play ball with you.'"
The question, Schulz added, is: "Who's going to back down first?"
The networks "may well feel like they're between a rock and a hard place," noted RonNell Andersen Jones, a law professor at the University of Utah.
"Capitulation might be perceived as abandonment of core components of press freedom," Andersen Jones said. "But the practicalities of lengthy White House news blackouts are also complicated, and refusing to cover major news at the highest levels of government might itself feel like a failure to serve the goals of democracy."
